newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Shooting at Sierra Leone airport.
newsitem.headline: Shooting at Sierra Leone airport.

text.p: Shelling or mortar fire broke out at the international airport near Sierra Leone's capital Freetown on Wednesday and soldiers in town spoke of a clash with Nigerians stationed there.
Residents and military officials said the cause of the firing at the airport, which is across an estuary from the capital itself, was not immediately clear.
Nigerian troops were in Sierra Leone under defence pact before a May 25 coup but have been reinforced as part of West African efforts to reinstate ousted president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
Soldiers at strategic positions in the city told Reuters that Nigerian troops had opened fire to stop some Sierra Leone troops who tried to make their way to the airport.

The sound of the firing caused panic in the centre of Freetown, which has been jittery since a Tuesday clandestine broadcast by Kabbah stoked fear of a fresh attack by Nigeria. Nigerian gunboats bombarded Freetown on June 2.

Sierra Leone's West African neighbours resolved on June 26, at a meeting of their foreign ministers in neighbouring Guinea, to press for Kabbah's return to power by dialogue and economic sanctions initially, but retained the option of using force.
Rebels, who took up arms in 1991, rallied to the coup and flooded into Freetown. They call themselves the People's Army.
Military ruler Major Johnny Paul Koroma has named rebel leader Foday Sankoh, currently under house arrest in Nigeria, as his number two.
